chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is nothing which the Angels attend except the horse-racing and the playing of the man with his wife.

key_terms.مُلَاعَبَةُ: Playing with / engaging in playful intimacy

ai.seo_question: What activities do angels attend according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this concise hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies horse racing (often associated with pre-Islamic gambling practices) and marital intimacy as the sole activities where angels are present. Shia scholars interpret this to mean that while angels generally depart during mundane or recreational acts, they remain as witnesses during the spiritually significant act of conjugal relations, elevating it from mere physical pleasure to an act of worship and divine companionship.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Ahmad Bin Is’haq, from Sa’dan Bin Muslim, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There is nothing which the Angels attend except the horse-racing and the playing of the man with his wife’.
en.sarwar: 1. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Ahmad ibn Ishaq from Sa’dan ibn Muslim from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
No other thing is attended by the angel as horse racing is and a man’s playing with his wife.’”
